question: Can the frozen nested-cylinder/shoulder relation be measured relative to a +Y cylinder axis without relying on global XY footprint rules?
model_class: one rotated +Y counterpart of the reviewed +Z two-cylinder planar-shoulder relation

ambiguity_or_fail_closed_conditions: global XY footprint used as a substitute
label or reference sequence used as a fact

constrained_hypothesis: The relation can be evaluated in an axis-relative frame for one fixed +Y control; every other orientation remains unsupported.

stopping_rule: do not generalize to arbitrary orientation
do not change public probe, runtime, helper, IR, SDK, manifest or provider behavior

existing: M32 supports the relation only for +Z. M27's +X/+Y rounded-slot evidence is a separate profile family and cannot be reused as cylinder-axis evidence.
missing_counterexample: a +Y relation whose global-XY logic would misclassify or cannot measure the shoulder
evidence.next_minimal_experiment: Completed by M33-002: one temporary +Y rotation matched axis-relative facts; the +Z-only reporter did not promote it, while +X, non-coaxial and missing-shoulder controls were unsupported. Any extension needs a separately frozen axis condition.
